title: Write jmap-scene-landscape-guide.md — prior art and competitive comparison
description:
Write a comprehensive landscape/prior-art comparison document for JMAP Scene that positions it against every relevant existing system and protocol. This is NOT a marketing doc — it's an honest technical comparison showing what Scene borrows, what it does differently, and why.

Sections to cover:

1. **Open standards and protocols**
   - OASIS (the fictional protocol from Ready Player One — what it imagined vs what's real)
   - Open Metaverse Interoperability Group (OMI) — their approach to interop
   - VRChat OSC protocol
   - IEEE 2888 series (interfacing cyber and physical world)
   - Croquet OS / Multisynq

2. **Corporate metaverse platforms**
   - Meta Horizon Worlds — walled garden, custom engine, no interop
   - Microsoft Mesh — Teams integration, enterprise spatial
   - Apple Vision Pro / visionOS — spatial computing without 'metaverse' branding
   - Amazon Chime spatial view — the 2D experimental variant

3. **Persistent virtual worlds**
   - Second Life — 20+ years, user-created content, land model, Vivox voice
   - OpenSimulator — open-source SL protocol reimplementation
   - Decentraland — blockchain-based land ownership
   - Roblox — game creation platform with spatial social

4. **Social VR**
   - Mozilla Hubs — browser-based, WebRTC, open source, shut down
   - Mozilla Social (the later Mastodon-adjacent attempt, also shut down)
   - VRChat — dominant social VR, custom avatars, Udon scripting
   - Rec Room — cross-platform social gaming
   - AltspaceVR (Microsoft, shut down)

5. **Spatial office/collaboration**
   - Gather — 2D top-down spatial video, the primary inspiration for viewHint 2d-topdown
   - Teamflow — similar to Gather
   - SpatialChat — browser-based spatial audio
   - Frame VR — browser-based 3D collaboration

6. **Games as prior art**
   - Doom (1993) — BSP trees, spatial state, networked multiplayer, 'will it run Doom' as litmus test
   - Gauntlet (1985) — 4-player cooperative 2D dungeon crawl, shared spatial state, the original couch co-op
   - Quake/Unreal — client-server authoritative model, the origin of modern game networking
   - Board games — Chess, Go, Settlers of Catan, Tabletop Simulator, Board Game Arena. Spatial objects with rules, turn-based interaction, the simplest possible Scene deployment

7. **What Scene does differently** (the synthesis)
   - State not rendering (parallel to VTC's 'call state not call media')
   - Protocol not platform — no walled garden, no vendor lock-in
   - JMAP not custom — builds on existing RFC 8620 infrastructure
   - Composable — Scene + Chat + VTC as independent capabilities that compose
   - Format-agnostic — visualRef/visualType, not mesh-specific
   - View-mode spectrum — 3D, 2D top-down, 2D side-scroll as a continuum not separate products
   - Simulation-agnostic — simulationUri decouples real-time transport from state management

For each system, cover: what it is, what it got right, what it got wrong or what's missing, and how Scene relates to it (borrowed from, diverges from, or is orthogonal to).
